ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a rough inclined plane, the inclined plane is inclined upward to the right, and object A is placed on the inclined plane; A is connected to the pulley at the upper right through a spring and a light string along the direction of the inclined plane, and after the light string passes around the pulley, it goes vertically downward to connect to the suspended object B; the angle of the inclined plane marked in the figure is 45°. Then reason: B is suspended at rest, and the pulley has no friction, so the tension in the string, that is, the pulling force of the spring on A, is T=m_B g. Analyze A along the direction of the inclined plane: the component of A's gravity down along the inclined plane is m_A g sinθ=3m_B g sinθ, and the spring pulling force up along the inclined plane is m_B g. When θ=45°, 3sin45°>1; when θ=30°, 3sin30°>1, so in both cases A has a tendency to slide down along the inclined plane, and the static friction force is along the inclined plane upward in both cases. The magnitude of the static friction force is f=3m_B g sinθ-m_B g. Initially θ=45°, f_45=(3√2/2-1)m_B g; later θ=30°, f_30=(3/2-1)m_B g=0.5m_B g. Because f_30 is smaller than f_45, the static friction force acting on object A decreases.
